newsitem.title: ITALY: Two metalworker unions back Italy gvt pay proposal.
newsitem.headline: Two metalworker unions back Italy gvt pay proposal.

text.p: Leadership of UILM and FIM, two of three unions representing Italy's engineering and metalworkers' sector, decided on Wednesday to accept a government proposal to end a protracted pay dispute with employers.
UILM president Luigi Angeletti and FIM president Gianni Italian said their executive committees had approved the proposal.
The third union, FIOM, whose members have expressed doubt about the government plan, was also meeting on Wednesday but had not yet reached a decision.
UILM, FIM and FIOM represent Italy's 1.7 million engineering and metalworkers in a sector which accounts for 40 percent of industrial output. Their two-year contract expired in June.

The government proposed on Tuesday extending the contract to 30 months. The employers would make a one-off payment of 512,000 lire ($316) paid in two instalments to cover the first six months, followed by graduated monthly wage increases totalling 200,000 lire ($124) during the rest of the contract.
Unions and employers' group Federmecannica have said they would decide by Tuesday whether to accept the proposal.
Their representatives are expected to return to Labour Ministry later on Tuesday to give a final answer.
Any settlement in the metalworkers' dispute is likely to set the tone for other pay accords and prove key to Italy's hopes of containing inflation.
